fromDeferred Behavior

fromDeferred is a FeatureCell API extension that converts a DeferredFactory<T> into a normalized StateType<T>, allowing promise-backed asynchronous results to be injected into the pipeline using standard state update APIs.
Note
fromDeferred is not backed by a standalone behavior; it is an alias provided by withCoreFromPromiseBehavior

This behavior operates outside of the pipeline and does not participate directly in Resolve, operator, filter, or reducer stages. Instead, it acts as a bridge that invokes a deferred promise factory, awaits its result, and produces a structured state envelope suitable for pipeline admission.

fromDeferred exists primarily as a migration and interoperability aid for engineers accustomed to Redux-style async action patterns, where state updates are often wrapped in promises and manually normalized before dispatch. It enables those workflows to transition cleanly into the SDuX model without requiring immediate architectural changes.

This behavior extends the FeatureCell instance by adding fromDeferred() (and its alias fromPromise()) methods that return a Promise<StateType<T>>. The resolved state envelope may then be passed directly to replaceState or mergeState.

When fromDeferred() is invoked, the deferred factory is executed within the FeatureCell context. The returned promise is awaited, its value is wrapped in a standard state envelope, and errors are normalized into pipeline-compatible error objects.

Because the promise is deferred, resolution is guaranteed to occur within the FeatureCell lifecycle. This prevents promises from resolving or rejecting outside of pipeline control, avoiding false state snapshots and orphaned updates.

Note

fromDeferred() is a single-resolution bridge, not a pipeline resolve mechanism. It exists to adapt externally managed or legacy deferred-based workflows into a normalized StateType<T>.

In most cases, it is recommended to pass a deferred factory directly to replaceState or mergeState and allow the Resolve stage to handle normalization automatically using the same deferred semantics. This approach avoids resolving promises outside of pipeline control, reduces indirection and boilerplate, and ensures that promise execution, error handling, and state commitment all occur within a single, deterministic pipeline boundary. Using the promise-based state APIs preserves the same lifecycle guarantees provided by fromPromise, while minimizing unnecessary steps that can complicate debugging or obscure the true source of state transitions.

Use fromDeferred() or fromPromise() only when you explicitly need to adapt or normalize a promise or deferred function result into a StateType<T> before submission.

Diagrams
Configuration

withCoreFromPromiseBehavior (there is no withCoreFromDeferredBehavior; fromDeferred is an alias) is configured by invoking the fromDeferred() (or its alias fromPromise()) method on an initialized FeatureCell. This method accepts a DeferredFactory<T> and returns a promise that resolves to a normalized StateType<T>.

Unlike resolve behaviors that execute inside the pipeline, withCoreFromPromiseBehavior operates outside of pipeline execution. It acts as a bridge that invokes a deferred promise factory, awaits its result, and produces a standard state envelope that can be injected into the pipeline using replaceState or mergeState.

The promise returned by fromDeferred() resolves exactly once and does not establish any long-lived subscriptions. Resolution is bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle, ensuring that deferred promises cannot resolve or reject after the cell has been reset or destroyed.

This API exists primarily as a migration and interoperability bridge for Redux-style patterns, where asynchronous state updates are commonly wrapped in promises and normalized manually before dispatch. In most cases, directly supplying a deferred factory to replaceState or mergeState and allowing the Resolve stage to handle normalization is preferred.

FeatureCell Deferred Integration

withCoreFromPromiseBehavior extends the FeatureCell instance with a fromDeferred() method, providing a bridge for integrating promise-based asynchronous logic into state updates without directly submitting the promise to the pipeline.

Unlike replaceState and mergeState, which accept finalized state inputs, fromPromise() accepts a DeferredFactory<T> and resolves it into a normalized StateType<T> value.

This method does not inject values into the pipeline automatically. Instead, it externalizes promise resolution and allows the resulting state envelope to be explicitly submitted using replaceState or mergeState. Resolution and commitment still occur through the standard Resolve and State stages.

Extended FeatureCell API
API Description

.fromDeferred(incoming)

inputs:

  • incoming: DeferredFactory<T>

returns:

  • Promise<StateType<T>>

Invokes a deferred factory and resolves its promise-backed value into a normalized state envelope containing value, loading, and error fields.

Promise resolution is bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle. If the cell is reset or destroyed before the promise settles, resolution is safely abandoned, preventing stale or orphaned state updates.

This API is intended as a migration and interoperability bridge for Redux-style or externally managed async flows, where promises are traditionally resolved outside the store and then dispatched as state updates.

Examples

withCoreFromPromiseBehavior provides a bridge for resolving a single promise-backed value from a DeferredFactory and converting it into a normalized StateType.

fromDeferred() resolves exactly once. The resulting state envelope must then be explicitly injected into the pipeline using mergeState or replaceState.

In the examples below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, a deferred promise is resolved using fromDeferred(), and the resulting state envelope is forwarded into the pipeline using mergeState.

Example 1: Resolve a Deferred Factory and Inject the Result

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();

    const deferredEmployees = {
      value: () =>
        Promise.resolve([
          { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
          { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
        ])
    };

    // Resolve the promise once and inject the result into the pipeline
    this.vault.fromDeferred(deferredEmployees).then(
      (incoming: StateType`}}<Employee[]>{{`) => this.vault.mergeState(incoming)
    );
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

const deferredEmployees = {
  value: () =>
    Promise.resolve([
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ])
};

// Resolve the promise once and inject the result into the pipeline
employeeCell.fromDeferred(deferredEmployees).then(
  (incoming) => employeeCell.mergeState(incoming)
);`}}
